title: Bartsch to Müller, 19/29 June 1631
author: Jacob Bartsch
source: Jacob Bartsch's letter to Philipp Müller written at Lauban on 19/29 June 1631, after Kepler's widow and children had moved there from Sagan: on the journey still to be made to Regensburg, Linz and Vienna, his logarithmic tables, the price of the *Ephemerides*, Müller's gift to his son, and the funeral poems for Kepler. The original is in the Bibliothèque de l'Observatoire, Paris (B, 1, 9; 89, 10. H. 9). Printed in extracts in *Nova Kepleriana* 4, ed. Walther von Dyck and Max Caspar, Abhandlungen der Bayerischen Akademie der Wissenschaften, Math.-naturw. Abteilung 31, no. 1 (Munich, 1927), 104–105.
transcribed_from: the page images of the 1927 printing.
summary: Bartsch, forced 'from the stars to the rakes', writes of Kepler's widow and children now at Lauban, his logarithmic tables, the price of the *Ephemerides*, and the poems on Kepler's death.

notes.on: from the stars to the rakes
notes.note: Puns in the Latin: *a libris ad liberos*, from books to children; *ab astris ad rastra*, from the stars to the rakes.
Benjamin Ursinus, who had worked for Kepler at Prague and was now professor of mathematics at Frankfurt an der Oder.
